facts_from_discussion: Petitioner has neither argued nor shown that he satisfied the requirements of section 7491(a).

Petitioner admits holding the two Prudential policies and having outstanding loans against them, admits that the policies lapsed in 2017, and raises no dispute about the derivation or computation of the amounts reported on the Forms 1099-R.

When petitioner stopped paying premiums, Prudential notified him that the lack of payments resulted in the termination of his loans and the underlying policies; the cash values of the policies were applied against the loans in extinction of both.

Petitioner's investment in each contract equals the premiums he paid; he disputes neither the amounts of the loans extinguished by the policies' cash values nor the amounts of his investments in the policies.
Petitioner has not argued or shown that his policy loans were not true loans; the borrowings carried an obligation of repayment when taken. He received no cash upon the lapse of the policies.
Petitioner resided at the Signal Mountain Property from January 1 until February 16, 2017, and rented it to his daughter for less than fair market value from September 15 through December 31, 2017.
Respondent introduced evidence that petitioner was obligated to file a 2017 return and did not do so.
Petitioner testified that he had "no valid excuse" for not filing except ignorance of the requirement to file while incarcerated; he knew of a general duty to file, having filed in previous years.
The court found no evidence of reasonable cause for petitioner's failure to file his 2017 return.

The IRS prepared an SFR satisfying the requirements of section 6020(b) for 2017, and petitioner failed to pay the amount shown on the SFR. Petitioner's only argument as to the failure to pay is ignorance of the requirement to keep paying tax while incarcerated; the court found that incarceration is not reasonable cause for that failure.

Respondent introduced evidence that petitioner had a tax liability for 2017, did not file a return for 2017 or 2016, and made no estimated tax payments for 2017; petitioner did not contest this evidence.
